attempts.label: DANDI:002014
attempts.paper_title: Aseptic, semi-sealed cranial chamber implants for chronic multi-channel neurochemical and electrophysiological neural recording in nonhuman primates
attempts.entry_title: Dopamine, spikes and LFP through an aseptic cranial chamber in a rhesus monkey (Choi et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: Of the paper's main findings, the larger dopamine rise after large than small reward cues and the spiking locked to the value cue held up in this data. Stronger beta suppression for large cues held only in direction (p = 0.108). The two-monkey recordings and the electrode yield, culture, drainage and bone growth results could not be tested, because the dandiset holds one session of one monkey. Spikes line up with the task only after their times are shifted by 11812 s, an offset measured in the data. The single-trial dopamine example and the single-unit waveform panels pass, but on weak criteria.
attempts.description: Tests the recording findings of Choi et al. (2025) on dandiset 002014, which holds one session of monkey T recorded through the paper's semi-sealed chamber. It compares dopamine and beta-band LFP power between large and small reward trials, aligns spikes to the value cue, and checks the unit's waveform and interspike intervals. The surgical, culture, drainage and yield results, and monkey J, are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Choi et al. (2025) from dandiset 002014

outcomes.notes: In trial 133 (1-based, a successful large reward trial) the SD of dopamine referenced at V over the 5 s after V is 2.02 times that over the 5 s before. Under the other reading (index 133, trial 134) the ratio is 2.04, with 36% and 46% of samples NaN. The test is weak. Of the 889 successful trials with a reference at V, the median ratio is 1.27, 64% exceed 1, and trial 133's ratio is above 76.9% of them. The criterion was written after trial 133's values had been printed.
deviations: The paper shows the trial as a figure with no measure; the SD ratio and its windows were chosen here.
The paper's trial numbering is not stated; both 1-based and 0-based readings are shown, and both match.

outcomes.notes: From V to reward, dopamine referenced at V averages 1.88 in large and 1.10 in small reward trials (difference 0.78 in the file's unstated unit, Cohen's d 0.19, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0035, 429 and 460 trials, 23 and 39 dropped for lack of a reference at V). Shuffling the labels within blocks of 50 consecutive trials, which keeps the drift across the session in the null, gives p = 0.0045. The difference is small in the first 2 s after V (p = 0.44) and largest from reward to 3 s after (difference 1.59, p = 0.0001, within blocks p = 0.0010); before V there is none (p = 0.50). It holds in the second half of the session (p = 0.0125) and not significantly in the first (p = 0.075). Without trial 1411, p = 0.0031.
deviations: The PCA dopamine estimate at V is subtracted, in place of subtracting the background voltammogram at V before the PCA; the two agree if the PCA model is linear, which the dandiset does not let us check.
The window (V to each trial's reward) and the test were chosen here; the paper states none.
Trial 1411, which the paper's large reward list leaves out, is included (one trial of 452); without it p = 0.0031.
Where dopamine is NaN at V, the reference is interpolated between the nearest valid samples if both lie within 0.2 s; none of the 62 such trials has them, so all are dropped.

outcomes.notes: With the spike times moved to the trial clock by the offset measured in the data check (11812.11 s), all successful trials have a spike within V - 1 s to V + 3 s, and the variance across 100 ms bins of the PSTH is 0.49 against a 95th percentile of 0.06 over random alignments (p = 0.005 with 200); 0.48 with the 7 ms lag also corrected. The rate falls from 5.63 spikes/s before V to 4.58 in the first 0.2 s and rises to 7.70 at 0.3 to 0.5 s. Large and small trials do not differ over 0 to 1 s (5.69 against 5.66 spikes/s, p = 0.90); the paper states no difference. The Plexon unit gives 0.17 against 0.06. With the spike times as stored, 42% of trials have a spike in the window and the variance is 0.01 against 0.03, so the claim fails on the file as published.
deviations: The spike times are moved by an offset measured from the data (the raw ephys located in the stored LFP); the file places them 11812.11 s early.
The spikes are those of the thresholded table (the paper's Zenodo file); the Plexon unit is a variant.
The paper states no effect for this panel; the criterion (spikes in most trials, and a rate locked to V beyond chance) was chosen here.

outcomes.notes: The criterion holds, but the evidence for a single unit is weak. No ISI is under 1 ms (9 of 101732 under 2 ms), and the mean waveform's trough of -56.4 µV is 4.79 times the SD across spikes at that sample. Neither part could easily fail. The shortest ISI, 1.562 ms, just exceeds the 48-sample (1.50 ms) waveform, so the detector's dead time excludes ISIs under 1 ms, and every one of the 101733 spikes exceeds the 40 µV threshold (smallest peak 40.3 µV), which nearly forces the trough above twice the SD. Above the dead time, ISIs per ms at 1.56 to 3 ms are 0.106 times those at 10 to 30 ms (Plexon unit 0.204), which fits a refractory period in most spikes but does not rule out other units. Only 54411 of the Plexon unit's 90912 spikes lie within 0.2 ms of a spike of thresholded unit 1 (101733 spikes). The Plexon unit has 1 ISI under 1 ms, 14 (0.015%) under 1.56 ms and 39 (0.04%) under 2 ms.
deviations: The paper states no measure for these panels; the 1% ISI rule and the trough-to-SD ratio are common choices made here.
The waveforms are read as microvolts, although the file states volts.

outcomes.notes: Beta power (13 to 30 Hz) falls after V in both conditions (median log10 ratio of 0 to 0.5 s after V to 0.5 s before, -0.158 for large and -0.125 for small, each p < 0.001 against 0). The fall is larger for large cues, but not significantly (difference of medians -0.033, Mann-Whitney p = 0.108; 452 and 499 trials, none dropped; shuffling within blocks of 50 trials, p = 0.19). Averaged over trials, as in the paper's figure, power over 0 to 0.5 s is 0.839 of the baseline for large (95% CI 0.782 to 0.903) and 0.885 for small (0.831 to 0.940), a difference of -0.046 (-0.125 to 0.036). No variant reaches p < 0.05 (15 to 30 Hz, p = 0.063; 1 s baseline, p = 0.108; 12 to 25 Hz, p = 0.19; windows of 0 to 0.3 s and 0 to 1 s, p = 0.59 and 0.84; without baseline, p = 0.17). The paper states no test for this panel.
deviations: The band, the filter, the power measure, the baseline, the window and the test were chosen here; the paper gives none.
The stored series, described as beta-band LFP, is broadband and was band-passed here.

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds one session of monkey T only (one NWB file). No recording of monkey J is in it or in the paper's Zenodo record, which also holds monkey T only. The monkey T part is tested by the Figure 8 and 9 claims.

The per-electrode background current and noise measured at implantation and during recovery, for 40 and 51 sCFEs, are not in the dandiset, which holds one FSCV electrode (c8ds) on one day. Not found in the Zenodo record either.
As for scfe-functional-yield; the electrode-level background and noise measurements are not deposited.
No mCFE measurements are in the dandiset or the Zenodo record.
The dandiset holds the FSCV of one electrode; the 24 and 15 functional CFEs and which of them showed dopamine signals are not deposited.
The culture results (IDEXX BioAnalytics) are not in the dandiset, the Zenodo record or the protocols.io protocols the paper cites.
The aspirated volumes per session are not in the dandiset or the Zenodo record.
The observations are photographs and surgical notes, which are not deposited.

findings.statement: The raw ephys and the spike times are not on the clock of the trials, events, LFP and FSCV table. The raw ephys is stored with a starting time of 0 s and a rate, and the spike times count from its first sample. Locating the raw c7b minus c5c signal in the stored LFP puts raw time 0 at 11812.11 s on the trial clock (correlation 0.98 to 1.00 at eight points, drift about 4 ms per hour). Without this correction spikes cannot be aligned to the task. The dandiset description says all data are expressed relative to the start of the Neuralynx recording, which the data contradict.

The absolute times disagree. On the trial clock the raw samples run from 12:06:44 to 17:12:20, while the Neuralynx header gives the recording as opened at 08:49:52 (the session start) and closed at 15:12:24, two hours before the raw samples end. The header span (22952 s) is also longer than the raw samples (18336 s).

The stored spike times of the thresholded units are about 7.1 ms after the spike troughs in raw c5d (in one 300 s segment of 1633 spikes, per-spike trough lags of -7.4 to -6.9 ms from the 10th to the 90th percentile, 98.8% within 0.5 ms of -7.1 ms).

The series "bipolar_lfp_series" is described as beta-band LFP but is broadband with line noise removed. Its values are already in volts, while it carries the raw int16 conversion factor (3.05e-8), which would scale them about 3e7 times too small.
The thresholded spike waveforms are stated in volts but hold microvolts (mean trough about -56), and the raw FSCV current is stated in amperes but holds nanoamperes (values around 1000).
The columns of the trial-aligned FSCV table (da, ph, m, iox) state no units, and the `good` column is true for every trial.

The subject description ("Two adult female rhesus monkeys were used for in vivo validation of the s-µIP device"), the session and experiment descriptions and the keyword "micro-invasive neural implant" describe the lab's micro-invasive probe study, not this paper's chamber.

The event table stores each event once per overlapping 60 s trial window, about five copies of each (7221 stored trial-start events for 1412 distinct ones), and its event times are not sorted. The Plexon units table's spike times are not sorted either.

The trial tags are all "initial cue display" and carry no trial type. Reward size and outcome can be rebuilt from the events, and they then match the paper's Zenodo trial lists except trial 1411, which the events mark as a successful large reward trial and the list leaves out.

The paper says the reward size depends on whether the target is at the top or bottom of the screen. The events code left and right conditions, and both reward sizes occur on both sides, so the target position that sets the reward is not in the dandiset.

The raw FSCV minute files are joined without their gaps (328 min of scans against 302 min of trials, placed from a single starting time), and the trial-aligned oxidation current cannot be located in them, so the raw FSCV's clock could not be established.

Only one session of monkey T is deposited. The data behind the electrode yields, cultures, drainage volumes and bone growth, and all of monkey J, are not, so eight of the thirteen claims cannot be tested.
